item.title: Claude Code vs Codex: Memory, Files and Config (2026)
item.description:
Claude Code vs Codex comes down to files and defaults more than features. Both are terminal coding agents that read a markdown instruction file when a session starts. Claude Code’s auto memory is on by default in local sessions. Codex memories are off until you turn them on.

Claude Code vs Codex at a glance

Claude Code Codex
Instruction file CLAUDE.md, and AGENTS.md in current versions AGENTS.md (and AGENTS.override.md)
Size limit Loads files up to 4 MiB; docs advise under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md 32 KiB by default (project_doc_max_bytes)
Built-in memory Auto memory, on by default in local sessions Codex memories, off by default
Where memory is stored ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ Under ~/.codex (memories_v2/ in a fresh home)
Skill folders .claude/skills/ and ~/.claude/skills/ .agents/skills/ and ~/.agents/skills/
Main config file ~/.claude/settings.json ~/.codex/config.toml
MCP servers .mcp.json in the project, or claude mcp add [mcp_servers.<name>] in config.toml, or codex mcp add

Sources for each row are in the sections below.

item.title: Codex Subagents: Built-in Agents, Custom Files and Settings (2026)
item.description:
What is a Codex subagent?

A Codex subagent is a helper that Codex starts to handle one part of a task. Codex runs several of them in parallel, waits for all of them, then returns one answer in the main chat. Each subagent does its own model and tool work. Its thread is shown in the app, the CLI and the IDE extension, so you can open it and read what it did.

item.title: Codex MCP: Add, Configure and Check Servers (2026)
item.description:
What is MCP in Codex CLI?

MCP (Model Context Protocol) lets Codex use tools that live outside it. An MCP server is a program or a remote service that offers tools, such as “search notes” or “save this fact”. Codex CLI, the desktop app and the IDE extension all load the same MCP servers, so you set a server up once.

item.title: Codex Skills: Folders, Install and Disable (2026)
item.description:
A Codex skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file. The file holds a name, a description and the steps for one job. Codex sees the name and description at the start, and reads the full steps only when a task matches. Put the skill in the right folder, and Codex finds it on its own or when you type $ and its name.

item.title: How to Install Codex CLI (2026): macOS, Windows, Linux
item.description:
To install Codex CLI, run one command for your system. On macOS or Linux, run curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | sh. On Windows, use the PowerShell line below. Then run codex in a project folder and choose Sign in with ChatGPT. Codex CLI is OpenAI’s coding agent that runs in your terminal, on your own machine.

What is Codex CLI?

Codex CLI is a coding agent from OpenAI that runs locally. It reads the files in your project folder, edits them, and runs the tools already on your machine. It is separate from the Codex web agent at chatgpt.com/codex and from the Codex desktop app. The official README lists the IDE extension, the desktop app (codex app) and the cloud agent as other ways to use Codex.

item.title: Codex CLI Config Reference: config.toml Keys and Defaults (2026)
item.description:
Codex CLI reads its settings from config.toml. The main file is ~/.codex/config.toml. Set a key there and every project uses it. Put a .codex/config.toml in a repo to change one project only. This page lists the keys people change most, their allowed values and defaults, using OpenAI’s configuration reference (checked 2026-11-10). Built-in memories are one key group; the Codex memory guide covers how they behave.

What is the Codex CLI config file?

The Codex CLI config file is a TOML file that sets the model, approval rules, sandbox, web search, memories, MCP servers and lifecycle hooks. OpenAI’s Config basics page says you copy only the keys you need into the file. Keys you leave out keep their built-in value, so a short file is normal.

item.title: Codex Memory: AGENTS.md, Memories and Add-ons
item.description:
Codex memory is two built-in layers. AGENTS.md files hold instructions you write, and Codex loads them at the start of every run. Codex memories, off by default, turn useful context from past chats into local files under ~/.codex/memories_v2/ (older setups: memories/). For memory that is searchable, shared across agents or kept on a server, add a hook-based plugin such as Hindsight.

Codex is OpenAI’s coding agent for the terminal, IDE and ChatGPT desktop app. Each session starts with an empty context window, so anything Codex should know must come back in from a file or a tool. Facts below come from OpenAI’s Codex memories docs and AGENTS.md guide, checked 13 October 2026, and from the Codex source and release notes up to 0.167.0 (6 November 2026). For Claude Code, Cursor and Copilot, see AI coding agent memory. For the two tools side by side (instruction files, defaults, skill folders), see Claude Code vs Codex.

item.title: AI Coding Agent Memory: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and More
item.description:
AI coding agent memory is how tools like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot carry project knowledge from one session to the next. The main mechanism is a plain instruction file (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or Cursor rules) loaded into every session. Some agents add automatic memory that saves lessons as they work. For more, teams add an external memory server. For Claude Code specifically, see Claude Code memory.

Every session starts with an empty context window, so anything the agent should know about your build, conventions or past mistakes has to be written down somewhere and loaded back. This page compares how the major coding agents do it, from their official docs, checked October 2026.
